entries.summary: Workflow SDK 5.8 runs workflows on a new execution engine, rebuilt for performance.
entries.text: Workflow SDK 5.8 runs workflows on a new execution engine, rebuilt for performance. Step-to-step latency is 12x lower, and large fan-outs, like running 256 steps in parallel, use 14x less function time outside your step code. This directly improves turn times for durable AI agents, among many other improvements. To get the new engine, upgrade to workflow@5.8.0 or later. New runs will use the new engine by default, and runs already started on an older version will safely keep running on that version. Make sure your steps are idempotent where possible to get the most out of this upgrade. Drastically reduced overhead In our benchmarks comparing 5.2.0 to 5.8.0, p75 step-to-step overhead fell from 85 ms to 7 ms. The median run, including 102 seconds of step work, finished in 111 seconds instead of 3.0 minutes. Running 256 parallel steps in a fan-out added 5.5× less overhead, 2.5 seconds instead of 13.5 seconds, and the median run spent 14× less time in functions beyond the steps' own work, 105 seconds instead of 1,446. A five-turn agent loop that streams its tokens through durable streams and calls tools added 0.9 seconds of overhead instead of 3.0 seconds, 3.3× less. Consult the benchmarks page for how we measure these numbers. Resuming after 1 second idle time went from 425 ms to 184 ms, 2.3× faster. Resumptions more than 5 seconds out might see slightly larger overhead. You can choose to keep functions warm for longer to optimize time-to-resume at the cost of additional compute
entries.title: Workflow is 10x faster, again

entries.summary: All Vercel Sandbox runtimes now use Vercel Managed Images (VMIs). Legacy runtimes, such as node22, now use the open-source images in the vercel/sandbox repository, distributed through Vercel Container Registry (VCR).
entries.text: All Vercel Sandbox runtimes now use Vercel Managed Images (VMIs). Legacy runtimes, such as node22, now use the open-source images in the vercel/sandbox repository, distributed through Vercel Container Registry (VCR). Sandboxes created with these now come with 64 GB of storage and use the same infrastructure as sandboxes powered by VCR. The universal image is released nightly, and rolling tags such as latest pick up operating system, dependency, and coding agent updates. Pin an image digest when you need a reproducible environment. Sandboxes created with version 3 or later of the JavaScript Sandbox SDK use vercel/sandbox/universal:latest by default. The universal image includes Node.js, Python, coding agents such as Claude Code and Pi, and common utilities. You can pull it at vcr.vercel.com/vercel/sandbox/universal:latest. Learn more in the Sandbox documentation. Read more
entries.title: All Sandbox runtimes now use Vercel Managed Images

entries.summary: Enterprise teams using Secure Compute can now create and manage AWS PrivateLink endpoints directly from the Vercel dashboard.
entries.text: Enterprise teams using Secure Compute can now create and manage AWS PrivateLink endpoints directly from the Vercel dashboard. Endpoints on Secure Compute live in your team's dedicated VPC and use the network's AWS region. They belong to the network and are shared by its connected project environments. Vercel Functions, Vercel Sandbox, and builds connected to the network can reach AWS-hosted backends over the AWS private network. Before you add an endpoint in Vercel, the backend must already be exposed through a published AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. Examples include RDS, Aurora, Redshift, Snowflake, MongoDB Atlas, and internal services behind a Network Load Balancer. In Team Settings → Networking, open your Secure Compute network and choose Add Endpoint from the PrivateLink tab. Standard pricing for new endpoints: Each Secure Compute network includes one AWS PrivateLink endpoint. Additional endpoints cost $30 per month each. PrivateLink data transfer costs $0.04 per GB. Read the Secure Compute PrivateLink documentation to get started. Read more
entries.title: AWS PrivateLink endpoints are now available on Secure Compute

entries.summary: With flags@4.5.0, projects on Vercel can use Flags Explorer and precompute without FLAGS_SECRET. That cuts out a setup step for new projects and removes the need to keep a shared secret in sync across microfrontends.
entries.text: With flags@4.5.0, projects on Vercel can use Flags Explorer and precompute without FLAGS_SECRET. That cuts out a setup step for new projects and removes the need to keep a shared secret in sync across microfrontends. Vercel signs Flags Explorer discovery requests and overrides, and the SDK encrypts flag values shown in the Vercel Toolbar with Vercel’s public key. Existing projects keep using FLAGS_SECRET while the environment variable is set or the secret is passed in code. Upgrading alone doesn't switch them to Vercel-managed keys. To use Vercel-managed keys for these features, remove the environment variable and any code that passes the secret explicitly. For local development, run vercel env pull. Precomputed codes created without a secret work only in the deployment that created them. Precompute without a secret requires Vercel system environment variables, which are enabled by default. Prebuilt deployments and codes that must work across deployments still need a secret; use FLAGS_PRECOMPUTE_SECRET if only precompute needs one. If you use a build cache, see the precompute documentation for the required configuration. Learn more in the Flags SDK documentation. Read more
entries.title: Flags SDK now works on Vercel without FLAGS_SECRET

entries.summary: Your agent can now manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP. Ask it in plain language to: Manage virtual models: Create reusable model IDs with saved settings, then list, inspect, update, or restore them.
entries.text: Your agent can now manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP. Ask it in plain language to: Manage virtual models: Create reusable model IDs with saved settings, then list, inspect, update, or restore them. Configure routing rules: View, add, and update team-wide rules that redirect requests to another model or block them. Set spending budgets: View and set budgets for your team, projects, and members, and configure defaults. To create a virtual model, for example, ask your agent: Create a virtual model named coding-agent that uses anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 with Zero Data Retention enabled. Your apps and coding agents using AI Gateway can then use vmc/coding-agent as the model ID. You can change its model or settings later without updating those clients or redeploying your app. To get started, connect your agent to Vercel MCP with team-level access and the required AI Gateway permissions. Your Vercel team permissions still apply. Read more
entries.title: Agents can now manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP

entries.summary: The Workflow SDK now lets you delete a finished run's stored data on demand.
entries.text: The Workflow SDK now lets you delete a finished run's stored data on demand. This feature gives you the ability to quickly meet compliance and security requirements when sensitive data needs to be purged from run payloads. Deleting a run's data deletes any inputs, outputs, hook payloads, and error traces for the run and its related entities. This does not delete the run's metadata: the run is still listed in observability. Attributes, hook tokens, and timings for steps and events can still be inspected. You can delete a run's data from the Vercel Dashboard, or via the CLI: You can also delete a run's data programmatically from your code: Deletion applies to finished runs only, so a run that is still going is skipped and keeps running. If you want to delete a run's payload as soon as it finishes, use the retention settings instead. Upgrade to workflow@5.7.0 or higher to use this feature. Learn more in the deleteRuns() reference. Read more
entries.title: Delete a run's data on demand in Workflow SDK

entries.summary: Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines is now available on AI Gateway. The small multimodal reasoning model is built for agentic coding, tool use, and knowledge work, with text and image inputs and text output.
entries.text: Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines is now available on AI Gateway. The small multimodal reasoning model is built for agentic coding, tool use, and knowledge work, with text and image inputs and text output. Inkling 2 Mini has 26.4 billion total parameters and 3.4 billion active per token. The model runs its middle layers more than once for every token, which lets it reason further before writing anything down and often reach an answer with fewer reasoning tokens. Like Inkling 2 Small, it is strongest on long-running agentic tasks. The model has a 1M-token context window, and reasoning effort can be set from none through max. Use thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Inkling 2 Mini in the model playground. AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more
entries.title: Inkling 2 Mini now available on AI Gateway

entries.summary: AI Gateway now runs canary audits against inference providers to detect when prompt content is read outside the inference path.
entries.text: AI Gateway now runs canary audits against inference providers to detect when prompt content is read outside the inference path. Contractual Zero Data Retention (ZDR) agreements and point-in-time security audits establish how a provider should handle your data, but production infrastructure changes continuously. Canary audits add a detection layer on top. Each canary audit run: Mints unique URLs that exist nowhere else, each mapped privately to a specific provider, model, and audit run. Sends prompts containing those URLs through the normal inference path, with ZDR requested for covered providers and non-ZDR pairs included as positive controls. Watches for traffic. A ZDR provider should never retain, inspect, or crawl prompt content, so a canary URL should never receive a request. Records any request to a canary URL, identifying the provider, model, and run for investigation. Canary audits complement contractual ZDR agreements and independent audits rather than replacing them. Read more about AI Gateway security and compliance measures in the documentation. Read more
entries.title: AI Gateway now runs canary ZDR audits

entries.text: （本記事は、英語版の就任発表の日本語訳に、花尾本人の就任のご挨拶を加えたものです。） Vercel日本法人の代表に、花尾和成が就任いたしました（東京拠点）。今後、Vercelは花尾とともに国内のチームを拡充し、日本市場への投資をさらに進めていきます。 弊社が10年以上前に公開したNext.jsを、日本の開発者の皆さまはいち早く使い始めてくださいました。そして現在、日本では三菱商事、富士通、U-NEXT、ディー・エヌ・エーといった大企業から、SANUや令和トラベルといったスタートアップまで、幅広い企業にVercelをご利用いただいています。 花尾はこの10年間、日本でソフトウェア企業の運営にリーダーシップを発揮してきました。前職ではPendoの日本法人社長を務め、それ以前にはHashiCorpの日本事業を立ち上げ、Pivotalの東京オフィスで営業部門を統括しました。 就任にあたり、花尾から皆さまへのメッセージをご紹介します。 このたび、Vercelの日本法人代表に就任いたしました花尾和成です。私は20年以上IT業界に身を置き、そのうち10年以上は、開発者が開発そのものに集中できるようにするプロダクトに携わってまいりました。この経験を活かし、日本の開発者の皆さまと、その先にあるビジネスの価値を最大化することに貢献してまいります。 Vercelには、CEOのギシェルモ・ラウチを筆頭に、日本を好きなメンバーが数多くいます。こうした仲間の後押しを受けながら素晴らしいチームをつくり、Vercelが日本市場にとってかけがえのない存在となることを目指します。そして究極的には、直接的にも間接的にも、Vercelが日本のあらゆる場所で使われている世界を実現したいと考えています。 今後ともご指導ご鞭撻のほど、よろしくお願い申し上げます。 ここからは、私（Nick Bogaty, CRO）が聞き手を務めた花尾へのインタビューをお届けします。日本市場にどのような可能性を感じているのか、Vercelへの入社を決めた理由とあわせて伺いました。 Vercelが日本でさらに成長できるとお考えなのは、なぜですか？ 日本のソフトウェア開発は、まさに転換期を迎えています。日本には革新的な企業が多く、高い技術力を持つ開発者の皆さまが活躍されています。一方で、多くの企業では既存のシステムが複雑になり、最先端のAIの導入がなかなか進んでいません。その結果、AIを十分に活用できていないケースもあります。 日本企業がAIのポテンシャルを引き出すには、AIを試す段階から本番運用へ進む必要があります。Vercelは、その一歩を後押しできると考えています。AIアプリケーションを大規模に、安全かつ安定して、効率よく運用できるよう支える。これはまさに、Vercelが強みを発揮できる領域です。 そして、AIにかかるコストをどう管理するか、どんなルールで運用するか、セキュリティをどう確保するか。いまやどれも技術部門だけでなく、経営陣にとっても優先課題です。最近お会いした経営幹部の方々も、こうした課題に取り組んでいると口をそろえておっしゃっていました。この点でも、Vercelは日本企業の力になれると考えています。 Vercelへの入社を決めた理由をお聞かせください。 複雑なことをシンプルにし、企業がもっとすばやく動けるようにする。以前から、そんなテクノロジーに魅力を感じてきました。Vercelなら、これまで私が取り組んできたことを、さらに大きな規模で実現できると思ったのです。いま、AIはソフトウェアの開発から

entries.summary: AI is now used in every part of a business, and as a result, companies send source code, customer records, and regulated data through inference providers.
entries.text: AI is now used in every part of a business, and as a result, companies send source code, customer records, and regulated data through inference providers. The assurance that no data is retained after processing is still publicly unverified. Payment platforms, cloud infrastructure, and most other layers that handle data this sensitive have a way to prove their controls to outside parties, and inference will follow the same path. Today we are introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway. A provider is labeled Audited ZDR only after an independent security firm tests its zero data retention claims against its code, infrastructure, and live traffic, then publishes the report. Baseten, Modal, and Wafer are launch partners that have already begun audits, and more providers are encouraged to join to help raise the bar for security and privacy. Audited ZDR builds on two steps we took toward stronger governance earlier this year: We launched team-wide Zero Data Retention (ZDR) so teams could route traffic exclusively to providers stating a ZDR policy. We completed our ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification, which put Vercel’s own AI systems under independent third-party audit. We are now asking inference providers for the same thing we asked of ourselves: independent verification. Why a contract is not enough ZDR guarantees rely on contracts and self-attestation. A provider agrees not to retain prompts or completions, and customers take that commitment on faith. For teams sending proprietary code,

entries.summary: Extraction models are now on AI Gateway. They find specific details in the content you provide, such as an invoice number or contact names, and return them as separate fields your code can use.
entries.text: Extraction models are now on AI Gateway. They find specific details in the content you provide, such as an invoice number or contact names, and return them as separate fields your code can use. ScaleDown Extract-1 is the first available extraction model. It extracts text values or lists of text values from text, images, and PDFs. You can use it to process invoices, contracts, and other records. Extraction is currently available through the AI SDK only. With ai@7.0.176 or later, use experimental_extract and the model ID scaledown/extract-1: Each key in fields has an entry in result.answers. If a field is not found, its value is null. Extract-1 returns confidence scores from 0 to 1 for matches, including individual list items, so you can flag uncertain results for review. For text input, it can also return character offsets showing where a match appears. To extract from a PDF or image, pass it as a file part in state: Extraction requests appear in AI Gateway logs and spend tracking. See the extraction quickstart for setup and authentication. Read more
entries.title: AI Gateway now supports extraction models

entries.summary: Vercel Flags can now block a deployment from reaching production if you’ve declared a flag in code but haven’t created it in your project.
entries.text: Vercel Flags can now block a deployment from reaching production if you’ve declared a flag in code but haven’t created it in your project. Without that definition, your app can silently fall back to the flag’s default value, even if that turns on a feature you meant to keep off. The Flag Definitions Present Deployment Check runs when a deployment is ready. If any flags are missing, the check fails and lists them in the results, where you can create each one before redeploying. The check reads your Flags SDK discovery endpoint. With flags@4.5.0 or later on Vercel, it works without FLAGS_SECRET; earlier versions still require the secret. To turn on blocking, teams on all plans can enable the check in their project’s Build and Deployment settings and mark it as required. See the Deployment Checks documentation for setup details. Read more
entries.title: Catch missing feature flags before they reach production

entries.summary: Provider headquarters sends your AI Gateway requests only to providers headquartered in countries you choose, so you can meet compliance and procurement rules about where your AI vendors are located.
entries.text: Provider headquarters sends your AI Gateway requests only to providers headquartered in countries you choose, so you can meet compliance and procurement rules about where your AI vendors are located. You can configure provider headquarters to be an allowlist of the countries to use, or a denylist of the countries to block. AI Gateway skips providers in blocked countries and routes requests to the rest of the list, so a model stays accessible as long as it is available in one of its allowed provider locations. Use provider headquarters with regional hosting and regional inference to control where a request is received, where the model runs, and who runs it. Set provider headquarters for your team Pro and Enterprise customers can apply their provider headquarters list to every AI Gateway request across their team. Configure the list in AI Gateway settings. Provider headquarters settings are applied automatically as AI Gateway adds models and providers. Providers without a headquarters country on record never receive your requests. Set provider headquarters per request On any plan, set headquarters in the gateway provider options to restrict a single request. Pass country codes for an allowlist, or prefix every code with ! for a denylist, as in ['!US']. If your team has a list, a request can only narrow it. entries.summary: Vercel Functions now accept inbound request bodies up to 20MiB, up from 4.5MB, in Public Beta. To turn this on, set the VERCEL_SUPPORT_LARGE_REQUEST_BODY=1 environment variable.
entries.text: Vercel Functions now accept inbound request bodies up to 20MiB, up from 4.5MB, in Public Beta. To turn this on, set the VERCEL_SUPPORT_LARGE_REQUEST_BODY=1 environment variable. The opt-in applies to the whole project in the environment where you set it, so you can test the larger limit on preview before enabling it in production. It requires the project's functions to use the performance memory setting of 4GB. It applies to functions on the Node.js, Python, and Bun runtimes, and to Routing Middleware. Functions and Routing Middleware on the Edge runtime keep the 4.5MB cap and return 413 on oversize bodies, so moving them onto the larger limit means switching to the Node.js runtime with runtime: 'nodejs', or proxy.ts in Next.js. When a project opts in, Routing Middleware receives request headers and metadata but no request body, enforced at the project level. Middleware still runs and still sees every other request header, so body-dependent middleware behavior is the one thing that becomes unavailable. This avoids sending the body twice, to both middleware and the target function, which would raise cost and time to first byte. When handling larger request bodies, read the body promptly and avoid holding it in memory to prevent backpressure and memory issues. Learn more in the Vercel Functions limitations documentation. Read more
entries.title: Vercel Functions now support request bodies up to 20MiB

entries.summary: Vercel has completed its ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification, meeting the international standard for AI management systems.
entries.text: Vercel has completed its ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification, meeting the international standard for AI management systems. This certification gives our customers confidence to ship fast with agents on Vercel, demonstrating how Vercel designs, builds, operates, and governs our AI products. Our AI management system covers Vercel’s underlying infrastructure and core AI products, including AI Gateway, Vercel Agent, v0, AI-based open source software and frameworks, as well as the people and processes behind them. Vercel’s certificate is available here, and additional audit documentation is available through our Trust Center. What is ISO 42001? ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the international standard for AI management systems and applies to any organization that develops, provides, or uses AI. An AI management system is the set of policies, roles, processes, and controls through which an organization consistently governs AI activities. The standard includes requirements for leadership accountability, AI risk assessment, lifecycle management, data governance, transparency, and continual improvement. The requirement that makes ISO 42001 distinct from security standards is the AI system impact assessment. Security frameworks cover how an organization protects information, but ISO 42001 covers how it builds and uses AI, including the assessment of how an AI system impacts the people it touches, and the benefits and harms that would result when that system materially changes. entries.summary: Coding agents can now use vercel help search to find Vercel CLI commands by describing a task in plain language. The search returns a list of matching commands.
entries.text: Coding agents can now use vercel help search to find Vercel CLI commands by describing a task in plain language. The search returns a list of matching commands. Add --with-help to include the help page for the first result in the same call. For example, vercel help search "roll back production" --with-help returns the options and examples for vercel rollback. Search also supports: API endpoints: When a Vercel API endpoint matches the task, search returns a vercel api command with the request path and placeholders for every required input. The agent can fill in the values without guessing the path. JSON output: Use --json to return search results as JSON. Combine it with --with-help to include usage instructions, options, and examples for the first result. Search recognizes common wording, such as “show” instead of “list,” and handles minor spelling mistakes. The CLI also includes a skill that tells coding agents to start with vercel help search when looking for a command. Vercel doesn't log your search text. Update to the latest Vercel CLI with vercel upgrade. Read more
entries.title: Agents can now find Vercel CLI commands by describing the task

entries.text: You can now check your team’s billing overview, review and download invoices, and preview upcoming charges with the Vercel CLI. All billing commands, including usage and budgets, are now grouped under vercel billing. entries.summary: Software development is moving from individual agents completing tasks to teams of agents working on more complex projects.
entries.text: Software development is moving from individual agents completing tasks to teams of agents working on more complex projects. A single agent can track its work in a Markdown file, but there isn't a purpose-built primitive for tracking tasks, delegation, statuses, logs, and completed work across many agents and subagents. We ran into this coordination problem internally and started experimenting with a shared message board as a primitive on two key projects: Our security agents: We deployed a swarm of agents to analyze our codebases for vulnerabilities, push fixes and updates, and now we keep track of their work via Board. v0's software factory: After seeing how well Board worked for security agents, we rebuilt v0's software factory on it, and it now merges over 50% of PRs. Along the way, we added multiple features like grants for different levels of access (for humans and agents), two-way sync for multiple tools (like Slack), and a lot more. Today we are launching Vercel Board as an experimental agentic primitive. It packages what we've learned about coordinating work across agent fleets and builds towards a future where multiple teams of humans and agents orchestrate swarms, software factories, and other agentic workflows. We built Board for our own needs, but invite curious developers to test it alongside us and give feedback. It is harness agnostic and fits well into existing multi-agent reinforcement learning. Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra, and LangChain

entries.text: Vercel Blob can now delete blobs automatically. Pass ttlDays when you write a blob and it is deleted that many days after upload, from 1 to 730 days. The TTL counts from the blob's upload date. Use TTLs for blobs you would otherwise delete yourself, such as session transcripts, exports, and temporary uploads. ttlDays works on put(), copy(), putImage(), multipart uploads, and presigned upload URLs. Every write result and head() response now includes expiresAt, so you know when a blob is due for deletion. setTtl() changes or removes the TTL of blobs you already have, one URL or up to 1,000 at a time, without re-uploading them. In Vercel CLI 65.16.0 and later, pass --ttl-days to vercel blob put, put-image, copy or presign, and use vercel blob set-ttl on existing blobs. Setting a TTL costs one Advanced Operation per started 60 days, on top of the write. A 7-day TTL costs one, and the 730-day maximum costs 13. Clearing a TTL and the deletions themselves are free. entries.summary: Today we're announcing eve 1.0, the open-source framework for building production-ready agents.
entries.text: Today we're announcing eve 1.0, the open-source framework for building production-ready agents. Since the public preview in June, we've worked with early adopters to prepare eve for 1.0, shipping 230+ releases and merging thousands of pull requests. With this release, eve is now generally available. We've made eve faster, expanded integrations, and improved observability. Security controls let you decide which actions need approval and what data gets collected. We've also made it easier for coding agents to build with, measuring that experience with a rigorous evaluation suite. With eve handling your harness and infrastructure, you and your agent can focus on building instead. Build production agents on a harness you own The harness in eve is the loop that calls models, runs tools, and delegates work to subagents. You choose the model, add or replace tools, edit instructions, and decide which actions need approval. The open-source Workflow SDK saves progress as the agent runs, so it can pick up from its last completed step after a crash. Multiplayer sessions and agent-to-agent calls are built in. For managed hosting, deploy your eve agent to Vercel. Vercel Workflows handles durable execution, and Vercel Sandbox runs agent-generated code in isolation. Build software factories that turn requests into tested pull requests, company brains that answer questions from your business data, or customer-facing agents in your product. Thousands of businesses already run eve in production

entries.summary: Agents are now users of software, doing work on people's behalf. Whether you're building the agent or the software it uses (API, CLI, MCP server, SDK), evals give you a way to measure how well that work gets done.
entries.text: Agents are now users of software, doing work on people's behalf. Whether you're building the agent or the software it uses (API, CLI, MCP server, SDK), evals give you a way to measure how well that work gets done. Agents probably missed your launch video and billboard on Highway 101, but they still go through the same funnel a human does to find and use a product: Discovery, Selection, Access, and Success. You can build evals for any stage of this funnel. Here, we’ll focus on the final stage, Success: whether the agent completes the user’s task correctly. That's more difficult to check than it sounds. An agent can place a “successful” order for a hot latte when the user asked for an iced one. The request worked, so the logs in your Observability stack look fine. And because LLM outputs vary between runs, one good manual test can’t tell you whether a fix worked. You need to repeat the same tasks and grade the outcomes, before and after the change. That’s what an eval is, a test you run many times and score. Here’s how we build one. The agentic testing pyramid If a test asks “did it work?”, an eval asks “how often does it work, and how well?” We group agentic software tests by how many LLM calls they typically need: deterministic tests (0), one-turn evals (1), and E2E evals (2+ across a whole task). This has turned out to be a great proxy for the effort to build them, the time they take to run, and the cost of running them. Just like in the practical test pyramid, the cheap and

entries.text: Alibaba’s Qwen4-Max is now available on AI Gateway. It’s a reasoning model for coding and long-running agent tasks, with image input, a 1M-token context window, tool calling, and structured outputs. With access to the appropriate tools, agents using Qwen4-Max can: Build 3D scenes and games: Work with Blender, Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot, running what the agent builds and using visual feedback to fix issues. Analyze documents and create reports: Work across documents and images to produce spreadsheets, presentations, and reports with source citations. Alibaba reports 35% fewer tokens than Qwen3.8-Max on its Work360 benchmark at high reasoning effort. Use alibaba/qwen4-max as the model ID: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Follow the setup instructions, then select alibaba/qwen4-max in your agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Qwen4-Max in the model playground, or explore all language models on AI Gateway. Read more
entries.title: Qwen4-Max now available on AI Gateway

entries.summary: Vercel Daemons can now send OpenTelemetry traces to Vercel Tracing, allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces.
entries.text: Vercel Daemons can now send OpenTelemetry traces to Vercel Tracing, allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces. Vercel provides each daemon with a Unix socket for receiving OTLP/HTTP traces and sets the socket's path in VERCEL_OTEL_SOCKET_PATH. Upgrading @vercel/otel to version 2.3.0 or later enables automatic trace export for Node.js daemons using the default configuration. The SDK detects this socket and sends the spans your worker records to Vercel. These spans are available through the Vercel CLI, which can search by service name within a project and return JSON for your agents. Learn more in the daemon tracing documentation. Read more
entries.title: Daemons can now send traces to Vercel Tracing

entries.summary: Vercel Token Pass now includes $150 of tokens per month (up from $80) for the same $30 per team per month.
entries.text: Vercel Token Pass now includes $150 of tokens per month (up from $80) for the same $30 per team per month. The credit applies to featured open-weight models served through AI Gateway, including Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Credit resets each billing period with no rollover. When it runs out, requests using standard AI Gateway keys or OIDC tokens fall back to the team's AI Gateway balance, while requests using Token Pass-scoped keys stop with no overage charges. Token Pass is an Early Access add-on for Pro teams, with limited spots and a waitlist when they fill. To connect your coding agent, run vercel token-pass in the Vercel CLI, or use a Token Pass API key if your agent supports AI Gateway. Subscribe to Token Pass in your AI Gateway dashboard. Read more
entries.title: Token Pass now includes $150 in tokens for $30/month

entries.summary: You can now scan code changes for vulnerabilities with Vercel Security Review in GitHub repositories that have not yet been linked to a Vercel project.
entries.text: You can now scan code changes for vulnerabilities with Vercel Security Review in GitHub repositories that have not yet been linked to a Vercel project. By default, Security Review covers all unlinked repositories the Vercel GitHub App can access in a connected GitHub account. You can limit coverage to selected connected accounts or individual repositories in Agent settings. Once enabled, each push to a covered repository automatically triggers a review of its code changes. Security Review checks commits directly in repositories with Security Review enabled, without requiring a Vercel project or deployment. When a push creates a deployment for a linked project with Security Review enabled, the review uses the additional project and deployment context. Connect the account in your team’s Git settings, then enable Security Review in Vercel Agent settings. Get started with the Security Review documentation. Read more
entries.title: Vercel Security Review no longer requires a linked Vercel project
